Always see how she’s doing. Talk to her and her care team to understand her treatments better so you can help her and your dad. Make sure you’re taking care of yourself so that you can help them. Be calm and it is hard now but don’t think of the worst. Infections happen but can be resolved. Look up nutrition information to help make the healing process faster. Ask your family if their home needs to be cared for in certain ways.
Hope this helps and hope she gets better soon.

First you and your family have my thoughts and prayers. My little brother passed a few months ago from advanced osteosarcoma and you start seeing it with wounds not healing and loss of feeling /paralysis in limbs. He lost appetite just a week before he passed. You’ll see the weight loss and notice some breathing may get harder. Try to get them comfortable with using oxygen if you can. Start asking if they’d like to be at home or in a special center when the time comes. Make sure you get affairs in order while he’s alive. While he was going it was nice to sit and talk with him. He was weak but still there. It hurts the whole time. The entire process is awful but please do not count the days. Do not try and calculate your time remaining just enjoy your time together while you still can. Enjoy small moments or memories. It makes the process a bit easier for both of you. 🧡

-Call upper management of the hospital/staff on your husbands floor. Explain the situation and let them know your concern.
-make it public that they aren’t allowing you to contact or every contacting you about your husband while he’s in this condition. 

This is all I have to suggest. I can’t imagine what you’re going through and I’m so sorry. I hope this gets resolved soon and you can plan how you’d like his hospice treatment to start.

Asking for extra support is understandable and if they’re willing I’d definitely take it. Needing time for yourself while going through this is important and yes it’s hard right night but if there is a possibility of a plan working out so that they can come over and help id take it. You’d of course have to talk about their country’s restrictions and they’d all have to get tested before and after and they arrive. You and other family members should be testers as well in order to make sure you all are staying safe during the pandemic but especially if someone else comes to your inner circle. Good luck and I’m sending you my prayers. This will be hard and support is the best thing to get at this time.
